I will still put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation, because that is my steady income and I have well water, so I can push yield if the weather turns dry. I do not like changing too much at once. Around here, if wheat fertilizer is too light, the heads stay small, and if maize misses the topdressing, yield drops fast, so I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose grain. Since my farm is 18 mu and some people in my family work off-farm, I also have to think about labor, so I will keep chili and cotton on smaller pieces. Chili can make money, but it needs more spraying and more watching. Cotton is slower but still gives me a steadier cash crop on a small area. I will follow what has worked in recent years here: improved or hybrid seed, enough base fertilizer, a clear topdressing plan, and irrigation timed to the key stages. For wheat I will use a little heavier nitrogen because I have irrigation. For summer maize after wheat, I will save labor and time with no-tillage seeding on the wheat stubble. Chili needs more potassium and more pesticide rounds because if disease and insects get ahead, the whole field becomes troublesome. Cotton I will keep moderate, not too much area, because it takes management. That is how I will balance grain security, cash income, labor, and cost this year.
